import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Reading the lead's report and diagram manifest; next I'll restructure and publish the canonical file.

Both diagram anchors match exactly one block, no external URLs exist, and all relative targets resolve. Building the file with a script so lead text and diagram fences are copied byte-for-byte.

Registration succeeded. Now the final declaration.

I've published the lead's report as `202611/waiting_on_remote_machine_agents/waiting_on_remote_machine_agents.md`. It is registered as `research:202611/waiting_on_remote_machine_agents/waiting_on_remote_machine_agents.md` (ref `file:explicit:d7fce2912b2df25fbb307be9`), and the commit is declared; the host makes it after this turn ends.

**How the file is organized**
- It opens with the title, then the research query, then the infographic (`waiting_on_remote_machine_agents_infographic.png`, confirmed beside the report), then `## Bottom line`.
- The other sections are, in order: Critique of the plan; How the five reports line up; Resolving the disagreements; Adjusted requirements; Recommended solution; Confidence and open questions; What I re-verified; Method and sources.
- Headings are not numbered, and there is no table of contents.
- The lead's "§3 row N" and "§4.x" cross-references would have pointed at section numbers that no longer exist. I replaced them with named in-document links, including in seven cells of the five-reports table. That is the only change to any table cell.
- Where a lead heading held code or punctuation, that text now opens the section in bold. For example, the turn-targeted waits section now starts with "**Defer `target=turn`.**"
- Nothing else changed in the lead's text, the two Mermaid diagrams or the captions.

**Diagrams.** The manifest's status was `ready` and its source matched the lead's label. Both proposed diagrams were placed, so none were omitted:
- `remote-target-pinning` → `#figure-remote-target-pinning`, after the paragraph in the launch binding and target pinning section that its anchor names.
- `recorded-remote-success` → `#figure-recorded-remote-success`, after the whole controller-side list in Components.

**Checks**
- The file has 4 Mermaid fences: the lead's 2 plus the 2 proposed ones.
- Each manifest fence appears exactly once, byte-for-byte, inside its own figure `<div>`. Each figure has one reference sentence linking to it.
- `pandoc` confirmed that all 46 links resolve, both in-document anchors and relative files.
- The lead's report has no external URLs, so nothing needed a curl check and no link was dropped as unrepairable.

One minor issue: `sase artifact read` would not accept the `research:` label for the diagrams manifest (it returned status `filtered`). I read the manifest through its `file:explicit:ba8da1c845e150fc4809270d` reference instead, and its contents were identical to the copy in the repository.
